analysis: The PR changes only AGENTS.md. Changed content: the deploy/ tree description now names cloudbuild-prod.yaml, host-setup.sh, a prod env contract and a dev overlay/swap. A new sentence says dev runs the same swap steps via deploy/gcp/dev/swap.sh and that a runbook change to a swap step also changes that script. The head excerpt is truncated at line 339 (the mutation checklist), so the remainder of the file is not visible in head. No code, protocol, auth, attestation, encryption, billing, or runtime configuration changes. TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 and T-052..T-058 are unaffected, and no assumption in the threat model is invalidated. The new text is an unenforced contributor instruction, so it creates no attack surface. The referenced deploy/gcp files are not supplied, so the accuracy of the description cannot be verified. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of risk. If the next pass sees the deploy/gcp/dev/swap.sh or cloudbuild-prod.yaml changes, it should check that production deploys keep requiring explicit human approval, and that the dev overlay cannot reach prod secrets or the prod project. The AGENTS.md text still states that production deploys require human approval and that direct local gcloud submit is rejected.
